narrative: OMX30 faces a mixed global backdrop: continental Europe rallies while US equities slide (-0.77% S&P, -0.92% NASDAQ), creating a near-zero correlation signal (-0.088%). Domestically, technicals remain constructively bullish—index 6.5% above 200-MA, MACD above signal, RSI 57.99 neutral—but Stochastic K=81.4 flags overbought conditions and mean reversion risk. The strong USD/SEK (9.979, +0.46%) is a tailwind for Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Ericsson, though NASDAQ weakness pressures tech sentiment. US 10Y yield +108bp supports Swedish bank NIM, while the sharp oil selloff (-8.00%) eases cost pressure. ADX 8.4 signals weak trend strength; confidence reduced 30% per rules. Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET could inject fresh volatility.
morningBrief: Open biased higher on European spillover and commodity stabilization, though conviction tempered by weak ADX (8.4) and elevated Stochastic. Watch 3,180 (50-MA) as intraday resistance; support at 3,085 (lower Bollinger band) and 3,123 (pivot). Export titans (Volvo B, Atlas Copco A, Ericsson B) outperform on strong USD/SEK; banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) benefit from higher yields but face refinancing headwinds. Oil's 8% crash is a net positive for industrials and consumer—monitor H&M B for sourcing cost relief. Real estate (Balder, Castellum) faces NIM pressure despite yield strength. Tech/Telecom sentiment dragged by NASDAQ −0.92%; Hexagon B and Sinch vulnerable to rotation. Copper strength (6.628, +0.94%) makes Boliden a core long; defensives (AstraZeneca, Essity B) should outperform if risk sentiment dips late. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is the key volatility trigger—print >250k could accelerate Nordic flows.
